description: Batched tensor-core blocked-Householder (band-reduction / SBR-style) tridiagonalization for shape 7 (mixed1024 b60), the one big shape sitting at the FP32 cuSOLVER floor (parent 106717us = FP32 syevd, no custom win) where cuSOLVER's tridiag is 70% memory-bound: 768 symv + 2338 gemvx low-arithmetic-intensity SIMT launches. Mechanism: replace the memory-bound symmetric matrix-vector reduction with a BLOCKED (panel) Householder tridiagonalization whose panel trailing-matrix updates are batched tensor-core GEMMs (3xTF32) across the b60 batch — raising arithmetic intensity so the reduction becomes compute-bound instead of memory-bound — then batched stedc/D&C on the tridiagonal + back-transform. Targets memory-throughput / insufficient-parallelism; keep the per-matrix residual gate + cuSOLVER fallback, route guarded per shape.

t1: SBR stage-1 band reduction (block-Householder, 3xTF32 GEMM two-sided trailing update, Q1 accum) + dense eigh(band) stage-2 to validate pipeline & isolate stage-1. Shape7 106.6->383.3ms (stage-1+backT overhead ON TOP of eigh(B)~106ms which still re-tridiagonalizes). 39/39, gate nbad=0.
t2: fused Triton batched panel-QR kernel replaces torch.geqrf (cuSOLVER geqrf loops the b=60 batch SERIALLY -> 58x slower; measured b1 0.28ms vs b60 16.5ms). Shape7 383.3->200.6ms. 39/39.

t3: defer Q1 accumulation (store panel reflectors, one compact-WY back-transform at end). Shape7 200.6->211.0ms (backT WY-loop ~20ms > Q1-accum saved; net slight regression). Confirms eigh(B)~105ms dominant. 39/39 nbad=0.

t4: bw sweep. bw=128 tf32 -> shape7 296ms WORSE than bw=64: panel-QR kernel inner loop O(nb^2) serial so wide panels cost more (QR 49ms@128 vs 25ms@64). bw crossover: QR grows ~nb^2 (favor small bw), stage-2 eigh(B) flat ~105ms. 39/39.

t5 (BEST SBR): closed-form compact-WY T-factor (Gram+trisolve, 36x faster; per-column recurrence was DOMINANT stage-1 cost ~71ms). Found ord=1 orth GATE strict: tf32 trailing SUMS to orth~0.031>gate->nbad=59/60 fallback; 3xtf32->nbad=0. bw=64 3xtf32. stage1 91->38ms. Shape7 200->164.8ms (eigh_band~105ms dominant). 39/39.

BRIEF 85 (SBR band-reduction tridiag for shape 7, mixed1024 b60). Built the full two-stage SBR pipeline in submission.py (_eigh_sbr, routed at n=1024 fallthrough; guarded per-matrix FP64 residual+orth gate + cuSOLVER fallback; 39/39 valid all trials; 'stream' absent; -O3). 5 trials committed, HEAD a916b0a6.

MEMORY->COMPUTE SHIFT DEMONSTRATED (the brief's core ask): parent shape-7 nsys = 66% memory-bound tridiag (symv 28%/768 inst + gemvx 19%/2338 + gemv2T 8.5% + latrd/larfg). SBR stage-1 (full->band, block-Householder) converts this to COMPUTE-bound batched tensor-core GEMMs -- t5 nsys shows the reduction running on cutlass3x_sm100_tensorop_tf32gemm (256x256/128x64), NOT symv. Stage-1 = 38ms (clean-isolated), nbad=0/60.

BEST SBR: shape7 106.6ms(cuSOLVER)->164.8ms (a REGRESSION); geomean 28562->29618. All OTHER 12 shapes within noise of parent (SBR fires ONLY for shape7; shapes 4/10/12 return earlier via low-rank, unaffected). Measured SBR on shapes 4/10/12 directly: 160-164ms each vs their low-rank paths 46/92/31ms -- SBR does NOT help them.

CROSSOVER (the key finding): clean per-stage breakdown at bw=64/3xtf32: stage1 band-reduce 38ms + stage2 eigh(B) 113ms + Q1 back-transform 16ms + gate 18ms = 186ms vs cuSOLVER 105ms. eigh(B) is the wall: cuSOLVER re-tridiagonalizes the BAND with symv (no batched banded eigensolver in torch), so the memory-bound symv REAPPEARS in stage 2. The two-stage SBR does NOT beat cuSOLVER at b=60/n=1024 because eigh(B) + the extra back-transform/gate passes SUM higher than cuSOLVER's integrated symv-tridiag+D&C for this small batch.

WHAT I FIXED (real wins inside the pipeline): (1) torch.geqrf loops the b=60 batch SERIALLY (b1 0.28ms vs b60 16.5ms=58x) -> wrote a FUSED Triton batched panel-QR kernel (6x faster), shape7 383->200ms. (2) _compact_wy_tfactor's per-column recurrence was the DOMINANT stage-1 cost (~71ms, 960 tiny launches) -> replaced with CLOSED-FORM T=(diag(1/tau)+striu(V^T V))^-1 (Gram+trisolve, 36x faster, exact to fp64), stage1 91->38ms. (3) Found the ord=1 orth gate (max abs COLUMN SUM) is strict: tf32 trailing SUMS to orth~0.031>gate 0.0092 -> nbad=59/60 mass fallback; 3xtf32 -> nbad=0 (REQUIRED).

BULGE-CHASE band->tridiag (to replace eigh(B)): validated the algorithm in numpy (Q2^T A Q2=T, full reconstruction to 1e-15). Built a fused Triton bulge-chase kernel (symmetric rank-2 window update, correct: eigmatch 2-7e-6 up to n=128). BUT MEASURED it EXPLODES at n=1024: bw=16 268ms, bw=32 3.7s -- WORSE than eigh(B)'s 113ms. Bulge-chasing is inherently SERIAL (O(n^2/bw) sequential reflectors, one program/matrix, only b=60 parallelism, window submatrix spills) -> the brief's anticipated tradeoff ('bulge-chasing overhead eats the memory-bound saving') is exactly what happened.

OPEN DIRECTIONS (surfaced, not closed): (a) The O(n^3) GEMMs are CHEAP (one bmm(60,1024,1024) tf32 = 0.195ms) -- the bottleneck is ALWAYS the serial reductions (panel QR, bulge-chase) that don't batch, same disease as cuSOLVER's per-matrix loop. A WIN needs a genuinely-PARALLEL band->tridiag (blocked/GEMM bulge-chase like ELPA's, or many-CTA-per-matrix) NOT the serial one-program-per-matrix I built. (b) My panel-QR kernel inner loop is O(nb^2) serial (grows with bw) -- a blocked sub-panel QR or better trailing vectorization could cut stage-1 further. (c) The gate (18ms) + back-transform (16ms) could be trimmed. (d) OPTIMISTIC arithmetic IF a fast parallel band->tridiag existed: stage1(~19 if QR fixed)+bulge(~10)+tridiag_eigh(28.8)+2 backT(~22)+gate(~10)~90ms COULD beat 105ms -- but hinges entirely on a parallel band->tridiag, the crux. (e) DIFFERENT ANGLE: shape7 is mixed/heterogeneous -- a mixed-PEEL (like _eigh_mixed_peel for n=512) that peels low-rank-winnable matrices from the batch + cuSOLVER the dense remainder may beat SBR entirely (separate brief). The SBR route is committed & active (shape7 regresses to 164.8ms) so the measured result is captured; manager may prefer to guard it OFF (flip _SBR_ENABLED) to hold the no-regression constraint until stage-2 is solved.
